newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Franz Fischler had launched a World Wide Web site on Internet today.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on the Court of Justice judgments.

Kubosch also said the Court of Justice Advocate General Damaso Ruiz-Jarabo Colombo had issued an opinion that backed Britain's argument that cigarettes bought in Luxembourg and shipped to Britain should be subject to full British excise tax.
In answer to a question, Kubosch said Commissioner Martin Bangemann had postponed a visit to the Czech Republic. It should take place before long, he said.
Kubosch also said Commissioner Bangemann would visit all the applicant countries to the EU before the summer holidays.

Asked about Tuesday's standing committee on food labelling, Kubosch said the decision whether genetically-modified soya and maize would be included in the directive scope would be taken at the next meeting that will take place early June.

In answer to a question on the Community banana regime, spokesman Gerry Kiely said that even if one country increased its production substantially above its regional quota, there would be no impact on the level of aid for other regional producers as long as overall production remained below the EU quota ceiling.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/317: Commission assists the modernization of Bari and Palermo airports.
- IP/97/318: Commission approves joint venture creating second national telecommunications operator in Switzerland.
- IP/97/320: Commission finances a self-training workshop on civil protection in urban areas.
- Speech/97/87: Speech by Commissioner Han van den Broek at "Give peace a chance - Women speak in Cyprus" meeting.
